body.name: \mathscr D_K,\mathscr D_{\lambda},\mathscr C_K,\mathscr C_{\lambda}
body.construction: Let \(\mathcal D=[a-b,a+b]\). For the finite-array experiment, \(\mathscr D_K\) is the collection of all randomized measurable Markov kernels \(D_K:\mathcal O_K\rightsquigarrow\mathcal D\). For the marked-Poisson experiment, \(\mathscr D_{\lambda}\) is the collection of all randomized measurable Markov kernels \(D_{\lambda}:\mathcal O_{\lambda}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal D\). Since \(L_K\in\mathcal A\subset\mathcal D\) and \(a-b\rho\in\mathcal A\subset\mathcal D\), replacing any real-valued estimator by \(\operatorname{clip}_{\mathcal D}(t)=\min\{a+b,\max\{a-b,t\}\}\) cannot increase absolute or squared loss pointwise; hence allowing arbitrary real-valued endpoint actions yields the same minimax infima. Separately, \(\mathscr C_K\) and \(\mathscr C_{\lambda}\) are the collections of all randomized measurable Markov kernels from \(\mathcal O_K\) and \(\mathcal O_{\lambda}\), respectively, to the measurable action space of closed subintervals of \(\mathcal A\), including degenerate intervals.
